excerpt: Why I-16, I-95, Abercorn and DeRenne carry so many Savannah crashes, and what to do if you are injured on one.
keyTakeaways: Savannah's high-crash roads — I-95, I-16, Abercorn Street, DeRenne Avenue, and I-516 — carry heavy commuter traffic, Port of Savannah trucks, and nearly 13 million visitors a year. Georgia's two-year statute of limitations (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and comparative fault rule (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, less than 50% at fault) govern how crash victims recover compensation, while federal trucking regulations provide additional grounds for claims against commercial carriers.

faqs.question: What is the most dangerous highway in Savannah, Georgia?
faqs.answer: By federal fatal-crash data (NHTSA FARS, 2020–2024), Interstate 95 recorded the most traffic deaths of any road in Chatham County: about 26 deaths in roughly 23 fatal crashes, with U.S. 17 (Ogeechee Road) close behind. I-16 recorded about 14 fatal crashes. Heavy Port of Savannah truck traffic and busy interchanges such as I-16 at I-95 and at Chatham Parkway add to the risk; I-16 near Chatham Parkway carried about 60,000 vehicles a day in a 2019 GDOT count.

faqs.question: How busy is I-16 near Savannah, and what has GDOT changed at the I-16/I-95 interchange?
faqs.answer: I-16 between Chatham Parkway and Dean Forest Road carried about 60,000 vehicles a day in a 2019 GDOT count, a dense mix of commuter traffic, long-haul freight trucks serving the Port of Savannah, and vehicles connecting to I-95. GDOT's 16@95 project is rebuilding the I-16/I-95 interchange with flyover ramps, widened I-16 to three lanes in each direction between I-95 and I-516, and added ramp meters at the Chatham Parkway and SR 307 on-ramps. Federal data count about 14 fatal crashes on I-16 in Chatham County from 2020 through 2024.

faqs.question: Is Abercorn Street dangerous in Savannah?
faqs.answer: Yes. Abercorn Street is one of the deadliest roads in Savannah: federal data show about 11 fatal crashes killing 12 people on Abercorn inside the city limits from 2020 through 2024, tied with U.S. 17 for the most deaths of any city road. The corridor carries heavy traffic past dense commercial development, and several of its intersections — including White Bluff Road, Mall Boulevard, DeRenne Avenue, and Victory Drive — have seen fatal crashes or carry red-light cameras.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33, you have two years from the date of your accident to file a personal injury lawsuit in Georgia. Claims against a government also need written notice much sooner: within 12 months for the state (O.C.G.A. § 50-21-26) and within six months for the City of Savannah (O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5).

faqs.question: What should I do after a highway crash on I-16 or I-95 in Savannah?
faqs.answer: Move to safety if possible, call 911 immediately, seek medical treatment even for seemingly minor injuries, document the scene with photographs if safe, do not discuss fault with anyone at the scene, and contact a Savannah car accident lawyer before giving recorded statements to insurance companies. Highway crash evidence can disappear quickly, so prompt legal consultation is critical.

faqs.question: Can I sue a trucking company if their driver caused my crash on I-16 or I-95?
faqs.answer: Yes. If a commercial truck driver's negligence — including fatigue, distraction, impairment, or violation of federal hours-of-service regulations — caused your crash, you may have claims against both the driver and the trucking company. Trucking companies can be held liable under respondeat superior for their drivers' on-duty negligence, and separate claims may arise from the company's own failures in hiring, training, or vehicle maintenance.
